question: In pharmacology, what do we mean by the term 'pharmacokinetics'?

options.A: How drugs are manufactured in a lab
options.B: What a drug does to the body
options.C: What the body does to a drug
options.D: How diseases destroy medication inside cells

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as the journey the drug takes inside you! It looks at how your body handles the medicine through absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. You've got this!

question: A community nurse notices many residents with severe watery diarrhea who all use the same stream. What is the best immediate step?

options.A: Advise residents to stop washing their hands after using the toilet
options.B: Report the cluster and investigate the water source as a potential reservoir
options.C: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy person in town
options.D: Close down the local hospital to prevent airborne contamination

explanation: When people sharing a water source get sick together, checking that water supply is a classic nursing move to find the culprit!

question: Which Nigerian agency relies heavily on routine disease reports and tracking to manage outbreaks?

options.A: Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)

explanation: The NCDC is our national frontline defense, coordinating outbreak responses using data sent up from local health facilities.

question: Which old-school stomach-emptying procedure is rarely used today because it carries a high risk of pushing vomit into the lungs?

options.A: Supplemental oxygen
options.B: Activated charcoal
options.C: Intravenous fluids
options.D: Gastric lavage

explanation: Gastric lavage (stomach pumping) is mostly history now because the danger of choking and lung aspiration is usually far worse than any benefit it brings.

question: Why can't nurses just use one standard diet plan for every single patient?

options.A: Because physical, metabolic, and lifestyle needs vary greatly among people
options.B: Because doctors legally cannot approve identical diets for two patients
options.C: Because food guides require a different plan for every day of the year
options.D: Because standard hospital menus never contain enough protein

explanation: Spot on! Every patient has a unique body, age, and lifestyle, so their meal plan needs to match who they are.

question: What is usually the main symptom of a small, uninfected vulval cyst?

options.A: No symptoms at all; it is often found during routine exams
options.B: Severe, throbbing pain that shoots down the legs
options.C: High fever and uncontrollable shivering chills
options.D: Continuous bleeding from the vaginal opening

explanation: Many small cysts don't hurt or cause any trouble at all. Patients usually only find out about them when a healthcare provider spots them during a routine checkup.

question: Which health promotion practice is most important for early detection of testicular cancer in young adult males?

options.A: Routine annual prostate-specific antigen tests
options.B: Frequent testing of post-void residual urine
options.C: Daily measurement of scrotal circumference
options.D: Regular testicular self-examination

explanation: Testicular self-examination empowers young men to notice hard lumps or changes early, when treatment is most successful. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h8)

question: You check a preliminary scan report on a confused patient and discover an unexpected fracture. What is your best next step?

options.A: Notify the primary care provider or medical team immediately for follow-up orders
options.B: Place the patient in strict isolation to prevent further bone damage
options.C: Discharge the patient quickly before the family sees the report
options.D: Wait until the patient complains of severe pain before telling anyone

explanation: Quick communication is key! Letting the medical team know right away ensures the patient gets proper care and treatment for that surprise injury.

question: What is the big benefit of using a head-to-toe approach for a physical exam?

options.A: It requires the patient to change positions constantly
options.B: It allows the nurse to finish the examination in under two minutes
options.C: It eliminates the need to inspect the skin
options.D: It ensures a structured and thorough assessment without missing body parts

explanation: Going head-to-toe builds a solid routine. It makes sure you never accidentally skip checking an important body system!

question: How is disinfection different from sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization takes less time than standard chemical disinfection
options.B: Disinfection is only performed on human skin and living tissues
options.C: Disinfection does not destroy all bacterial spores like sterilization does
options.D: Sterilization uses chemical agents while disinfection only uses heat

explanation: Spot on! Sterilization is the heavy-duty process that wipes out every single trace of life, including tough spores. Disinfection cleans up most germs, but leaves spores behind.

question: Why is community education and reducing stigma such a vital part of nursing care for immune conditions?

options.A: It encourages people to seek testing and treatment early without fear.
options.B: It stops patients from needing physical check-ups at the clinic.
options.C: It replaces the need for nutritional supplements in rural areas.
options.D: It lowers the cost of manufacturing hospital equipment.

explanation: Brilliant! When we break down stigma, patients feel safe to get tested and start life-saving treatment early.

question: Why is lung surfactant so vital for a newborn's breathing?

options.A: It warms up the cold air entering the nose
options.B: It fights off chest infections
options.C: It pumps fluid out of the tiny airways
options.D: It reduces surface tension in the alveoli to keep them open

explanation: Surfactant acts like a slick coating inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) so they don't stick shut and collapse every time the baby breathes out.

question: How can clinical nurses positively influence waste management practices on their wards?

options.A: By writing national environmental laws in parliament
options.B: By driving the municipal garbage trucks on weekends
options.C: By buying new incineration machines for the hospital
options.D: By acting as role models and teaching junior staff correct sorting

explanation: Spot on! Your daily good habits teach junior colleagues and students how to do things the right way.

question: Why do community health nurses spend time educating the public?

options.A: To replace formal school teachers in local primary classrooms
options.B: To empower individuals and groups with knowledge to prevent illness
options.C: To test public speaking skills during routine ward rounds
options.D: To fulfill mandatory administrative writing quotas

explanation: Spot on! Education is one of our most powerful tools. When people understand how diseases spread and how to live healthily, they can take charge of their own wellbeing.

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on personal opinion in a nursing paper?

options.A: Instructors simply do not like reading personal thoughts
options.B: Clinical claims must rest on verifiable evidence
options.C: Personal opinions are always grammatically incorrect
options.D: It takes too much time to write out opinions

explanation: Spot on! Nursing is an evidence-based field, meaning we always back our care with proven facts rather than just guesswork.

question: Why do social factors like poverty play such a big role in NCDs?

options.A: They ensure that patients always adhere strictly to their medication regimen
options.B: They directly cause genetic mutations that trigger cancer within weeks
options.C: They limit access to healthy foods, safe exercise spaces, and proper healthcare
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of developing infectious diseases

explanation: Exactly! When money is tight, it becomes much harder to afford nutritious food, find safe places to exercise, or visit the clinic early for check-ups.

question: What is the main difference between shear and friction in skin breakdown?

options.A: Shear only happens on the heels, whereas friction only happens on the sacrum.
options.B: Shear happens when bones slide inside while skin stays stuck; friction is just surface rubbing.
options.C: Shear damages bone tissue, whereas friction only damages hair follicles.
options.D: Shear is caused by moisture, whereas friction is caused by lack of protein.

explanation: Friction is like skin rubbing against bedsheets, but shear happens when the skeleton slides down while the outer skin stays put, twisting the blood vessels inside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is a great non-drug way to handle behavioral symptoms in a patient?

options.A: Restricting all visits from family and close friends
options.B: Administering high doses of sedating antipsychotic drugs
options.C: Moving the patient to a completely unfamiliar location daily
options.D: Maintaining predictable daily routines in a calm environment

explanation: You got it! Calm settings and steady daily routines do wonders to soothe patients and lower anxiety without needing extra pills. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h5)

question: Which behavior change in a child should make a nurse check for possible abuse?

options.A: Sudden and extreme withdrawal from social interactions
options.B: Showing normal reluctance to share toys with peers
options.C: Expressing sadness after losing a family pet
options.D: Preferring quiet independent reading over active games

explanation: A drastic shift like sudden, severe withdrawal is a big red flag that something scary might be happening at home.

question: A patient starts coughing violently and turns pale while you are inserting a feeding tube. What should you do first?

options.A: Push the tube in faster to get it past the vocal cords
options.B: Give the patient a large cup of cold water to drink
options.C: Listen with your stethoscope over the left chest wall
options.D: Pull the tube back immediately because it is in the airway

explanation: Coughing and color changes indicate the tube has entered the trachea, requiring immediate withdrawal to restore breathing. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the main catch or limitation of chemical buffer systems?

options.A: They only bind or release ions temporarily without removing them
options.B: They take days to reach peak chemical effectiveness
options.C: They function exclusively inside the cells of skeletal muscle
options.D: They require active nervous system input to initiate action

explanation: Buffers are great first responders, but they only hold onto excess ions temporarily. To truly get rid of acids or bases, the lungs and kidneys have to step in.

question: A patient with urge incontinence is starting a bladder retraining program. What is the right instruction to give them?

options.A: Stop doing pelvic floor exercises completely
options.B: Hold urine for as long as possible until severe pain occurs
options.C: Drink large amounts of water only right before bedtime
options.D: Urinate on a strict schedule, slowly increasing the time between trips

explanation: Bladder retraining uses a set schedule that slowly stretches out the time between bathroom breaks, helping the bladder hold more without sudden spasms.

question: Besides anxiety, what is another common medical use for minor tranquilizers?

options.A: Long-term cure for bacterial infections
options.B: Reversing opioid overdoses
options.C: Stimulating appetite in cachexia
options.D: Alcohol withdrawal management

explanation: Doctors often prescribe benzodiazepines during alcohol withdrawal to keep dangerous tremors and seizures away. You're doing great!

question: What is the primary goal of triage in an emergency department?

options.A: To sort patients based on the severity of their condition
options.B: To assign a private room to every arriving patient
options.C: To collect insurance and billing information promptly
options.D: To discharge patients who have minor complaints quickly

explanation: Triage allows nurses to prioritize care so that the most critically ill or injured patients receive immediate attention. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h1)

question: Why do clinical meal plans usually still allow tiny amounts of natural sodium?

options.A: Natural sodium has no effect on human blood pressure
options.B: Basic physiological functions still require small amounts of sodium
options.C: Patients will otherwise refuse to eat any hospital meals
options.D: It helps preserve food for longer periods without refrigeration

explanation: Spot on! Our bodies actually need a little bit of sodium to keep our cells working right, so zero sodium is rarely the goal.

question: What is the primary purpose of irrigating a fresh wound with normal saline?

options.A: To wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.B: To numb the pain temporarily
options.C: To close the skin edges tightly
options.D: To stop bleeding from large arteries

explanation: High-volume fluid irrigation physically flushes out contaminants that could otherwise cause a localized infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the official color of the standard ADR reporting form used by NAFDAC?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: White
options.C: Green
options.D: Blue

explanation: You'll see this often in practice! The NAFDAC Yellow Form is the standard, easily recognizable document used across Nigeria for reporting bad drug reactions.

question: A 14-year-old pregnant girl is at the clinic. Based on her body's development, she is at the highest risk for which complication?

options.A: Enhanced muscular strength in the pelvic floor
options.B: Severe tearing and tissue trauma during labor
options.C: Permanent widening of the pelvic brim
options.D: Rapid bone density increase from pregnancy hormones

explanation: Young reproductive tissues tear much easier because they are not fully grown or stretchy enough for birth yet.

question: What happens to a vaccine when the cold chain is broken?

options.A: It becomes stronger and requires a smaller dose
options.B: It changes color but remains completely safe to use
options.C: It loses its potency and fails to protect the patient
options.D: It turns into a dangerous liquid poison immediately

explanation: Temperature exposures outside the recommended range permanently destroy the active components of the vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: On a standard ECG tracing, what does the QRS complex show us?

options.A: Ventricular recovery
options.B: Sinoatrial node firing
options.C: Ventricular depolarization
options.D: Atrial repolarization

explanation: Think of the QRS complex as the big electrical wave rushing through the lower chambers (ventricles), telling them it's time to squeeze and pump blood out to the body!

question: During a gastric lavage, a patient suddenly turns cyanotic, coughs hard, and has a drop in oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ask the patient to take deep breaths through their nose
options.B: Stop the procedure immediately and suction the airway
options.C: Instill more wash fluid to clear out any remaining blockages
options.D: Remove the protective endotracheal tube right away

explanation: These signs point to fluid aspiration into the lungs, requiring an immediate halt to fluid instillation and clearing of the airway to restore breathing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary aim of culturally sensitive nutrition counseling in nursing?

options.A: Forcing patients to abandon their cultural heritage completely
options.B: Convincing doctors to change hospital meal timetables
options.C: Replacing all local dishes with imported western food items
options.D: Finding acceptable local food substitutes that maintain good nutrition

explanation: We don't need to fight a patient's culture! Instead, we work with what they have, suggesting safe, affordable local foods that provide the exact same nutrients.

question: A 36-week pregnant mum asks why the nurse wants her to identify a blood donor and save transport money. How should the nurse reply?

options.A: These steps ensure quick action if an unexpected emergency like heavy bleeding occurs.
options.B: The hospital requires these items as a deposit before admitting any woman in labor.
options.C: Blood donations are used to test your own blood type one final time.
options.D: It is a legal formality that has no real impact on your actual delivery outcome.

explanation: Having cash and a willing blood donor ready beforehand can literally save a life if heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) happens suddenly.

question: Why must nurses always ask patients if they are taking traditional or herbal remedies along with prescribed drugs?

options.A: To calculate the patient's daily fluid intake and output accurately
options.B: To prevent dangerous herb-drug interactions that could harm the patient
options.C: To prove that orthodox medicine is superior to cultural treatments
options.D: To report traditional healers to the local pharmaceutical board

explanation: Herbs are powerful! Mixing them with hospital medications can cause bad reactions or stop the prescribed drug from working.

question: Which condition is a common indication for a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: Acute muscle strains
options.B: Superficial skin lacerations
options.C: Complex bone fractures
options.D: Simple ligament sprains

explanation: CT scans are especially helpful for viewing complicated, multi-part fractures and seeing how bone fragments line up within a joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of these beta-blockers are commonly prescribed in heart failure?

options.A: Carvedilol and metoprolol succinate
options.B: Atropine and adrenaline sulfate
options.C: Salbutamol and formoterol fumarate
options.D: Atenolol and propranolol hydrochloride

explanation: You're crushing it! Carvedilol and metoprolol succinate are proven champions in heart failure care, helping protect the heart over the long haul.

question: What is the main job of the accessory organs in our digestive system?

options.A: To provide chemical secretions like enzymes and bile
options.B: To absorb all water from digested food materials
options.C: To physically push food forward using strong muscles
options.D: To serve as the primary storage tube for waste

explanation: Think of accessory organs as your digestive helpers! Instead of holding food inside a tube like the stomach or intestines, they pump in helpful chemical juices—like enzymes and bile—to break down your food.

question: Why is it helpful to involve patients in small self-care tasks during recovery?

options.A: It forces the body to skip the alarm stage of the GAS model
options.B: It guarantees that no complications will ever develop
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any medications
options.D: It restores a sense of personal control and reduces helplessness

explanation: Active participation empowers patients, countering the loss of control often brought on by severe illness and hospitalization. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h6)

question: How do you properly check the function of cranial nerve XI (the spinal accessory nerve) in an adult?

options.A: By checking if the patient can stick out their tongue straight
options.B: By shining a bright light into both of the patient's eyes
options.C: By asking the patient to shrug their shoulders against resistance
options.D: By testing the patient's ability to hear a whispered voice

explanation: Just place your hands on their shoulders and ask them to shrug against your push. That tests cranial nerve XI easily!

question: Why is proper cleaning and drying of nebulizer equipment so critical for patient safety?

options.A: Dirty equipment will permanently break the air compressor motor
options.B: Washing prevents the plastic mask from changing color over time
options.C: Moist plastic parts easily grow harmful bacteria that can cause lung infections
options.D: Leftover medication residue turns into a solid metal inside the tube

explanation: Wet nebulizer cups are breeding grounds for germs, which the patient would inhale directly into their lungs during the next treatment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: How should numbers inside a research table column normally be aligned?

options.A: To the right or by decimal points
options.B: Centered with uneven spacing
options.C: To the extreme left margin
options.D: Diagonally across the cells

explanation: Right-aligning or lining up numbers by their decimal points makes it super easy to compare sizes up and down at a glance.

question: As a night nurse, what is the best way to help reduce environmental stress for patients on a busy ward?

options.A: Leave the overhead fluorescent lights on so staff can monitor safely
options.B: Turn up the monitor alarm volumes so they can be heard down the hall
options.C: Cluster nursing care activities to allow longer periods of uninterrupted sleep
options.D: Encourage visitors to stay past visiting hours to keep spirits high

explanation: By grouping your tasks together (like doing vitals and giving meds at the same time), you let patients sleep peacefully without waking them up every hour. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: At what fill level should a clinical waste bag be tied up and removed?

options.A: Completely packed to the brim
options.B: Whenever the shift ends
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: One-quarter full

explanation: Correct! Tying bags at 3/4 capacity stops them from overflowing, spilling, or tearing when you carry them. Stay safe out there!

question: How does the World Health Organization (WHO) define a safe injection?

options.A: One that does not harm the recipient, provider, or community
options.B: One that uses only glass syringes and metal needles
options.C: One that is administered exclusively by registered nurses
options.D: One that costs less than standard oral medications

explanation: Think of the WHO definition as a circle of safety: it covers the patient getting the drug, the nurse giving it, and the public handling the waste.

question: How do support groups primarily help members overcome internalized stigma?

options.A: By providing legal documents to sue community members who spread gossip
options.B: By connecting them with thriving peers who challenge false beliefs through shared experiences
options.C: By hiding the medical diagnosis from all family and healthcare providers
options.D: By relocating patients to secret towns where nobody knows about the virus

explanation: Seeing healthy, confident peers living openly breaks down the false idea that the diagnosis destroys a person's worth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h4)

question: How does social stigma make the problem of unsafe abortions even worse?

options.A: It forces women to hide their condition and delay seeking safe help
options.B: It prevents healthcare workers from learning basic nursing skills
options.C: It causes severe hormonal imbalances that mimic pregnancy complications
options.D: It directly reduces the availability of surgical equipment in hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of judgment and shame makes patients wait too long or use dangerous home remedies instead of coming to us for safe care.

question: You notice a ventilated patient has no breath sounds on the left side and uneven chest movement. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The humidifier water chamber is completely empty
options.B: The ventilator circuit tubing has a small external leak
options.C: The patient is experiencing a sudden drop in blood sugar
options.D: The breathing tube has slipped into the right main bronchus

explanation: Because the right main bronchus is wider and straighter, breathing tubes often slip too far down into it. This accidentally ventilates only the right lung, leaving the left side quiet. Always check tube placement!

question: A student nurse sees a cleaner throwing used syringes into a normal paper trash bin. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Report the entire ward to the police without speaking to the staff first
options.B: Start throwing all hospital refuse directly out of the ward window
options.C: Ignore the practice since waste disposal is solely the job of orderlies
options.D: Correct the practice immediately, retrain the staff, and ensure proper bins are used

explanation: You got it! As a nurse, you are a safety leader. Educating your team and correcting safety slips right away keeps everyone safe.

question: What do government rehabilitation programs usually provide for displaced or vulnerable people?

options.A: Exemption from all federal and state laws
options.B: Vocational skills training and temporary shelter
options.C: Free commercial real estate deeds
options.D: Mandatory relocation to a foreign country

explanation: You got it! Rehabilitation programs help stabilize vulnerable people by giving them a safe place to stay and practical skills to stand on their own feet.

question: Why do patients in severe anaphylaxis often feel dizzy or faint?

options.A: Blood pressure crashes because fluid leaks out of widened blood vessels
options.B: Heavy sweating causes bad dehydration
options.C: The brain gets too much oxygen from fast breathing
options.D: The heart beats too slowly to pump blood

explanation: Blood vessels suddenly open wide and leak fluid, causing blood pressure to drop low. This starves the brain of blood flow, leading to dizziness.

question: Why is early recognition by the nurse vital in oncologic emergencies?

options.A: It shortens the patient's hospital stay to one day
options.B: It completely cures the underlying cancer
options.C: It prevents permanent organ damage and death
options.D: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests

explanation: Because these conditions develop rapidly and threaten life, catching them early stops the cascade toward permanent organ failure. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h1)

question: If you don't have a tissue handy and suddenly need to cough, what should you do?

options.A: Cough into your inner elbow
options.B: Cough directly into the open air
options.C: Turn your head toward the nearest wall
options.D: Cover your mouth with both bare hands

explanation: Brilliant! Coughing into your elbow keeps the droplets off your hands. If you cough into your hands, you'll just transfer those germs to every door handle and chart you touch!

question: A patient tells you she uses petroleum jelly as a lubricant with her latex condoms. What should be your immediate nursing advice?

options.A: Confirm that petroleum jelly is the ideal choice for extra slip
options.B: Warn her that oil-based lubricants weaken latex and can cause breakage
options.C: Advise her to microwave the jelly first to make it safe for use
options.D: Suggest she switch to oil-based spermicide creams instead

explanation: Brilliant! Oil-based products break down latex rubber super fast, leading to tears. Water-based lube is always the safe choice here!

question: Why is checking daily on chronic illnesses so important in a home setting?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests entirely
options.B: It proves to the insurance company that nursing visits are unnecessary
options.C: It completely cures chronic conditions without the need for medications
options.D: It helps catch early warning signs before a hospital admission is needed

explanation: Exactly right! Catching small changes early lets you and the medical team step in quickly, keeping the patient out of the hospital ward. Excellent clinical intuition!

question: Why must patients constantly rotate their injection sites?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.B: To prevent localized skin hardening and altered drug absorption
options.C: To stop the needle from becoming dull during repeated use
options.D: To ensure the medication reaches the bloodstream much faster

explanation: Using the exact same spot over and over can cause fatty lumps (lipohypertrophy) and mess up how the drug is absorbed. Moving around keeps the skin healthy!

question: Which of these tools do you need on your clean workspace when mixing a topical dilution?

options.A: A standard household kitchen spoon
options.B: A clean mixing tile and spatula
options.C: A sterile surgical scalpel
options.D: A glass measuring cup for oral liquids

explanation: A clean flat tile and a spatula give you a nice, sanitary surface to blend your creams smoothly.

question: What is the specific function of the auditory association area?

options.A: To register the raw pitch and volume of a loud noise
options.B: To interpret the meaning of sounds and spoken words
options.C: To control the physical movement of the tiny ear bones
options.D: To maintain balance and posture during head rotation

explanation: While the primary cortex hears the noise, the association area figures out what the noise actually means, such as recognizing speech. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h4)

question: A patient gets confused by heavy medical jargon you used. Where did the communication break down?

options.A: During the decoding phase
options.B: During the feedback generation
options.C: During the sender's encoding
options.D: During the channel selection

explanation: Exactly! Decoding is when the listener tries to make sense of your words—complex medical terms make this step tough.

question: According to Herzberg, which of the following is considered a hygiene factor?

options.A: Taking on extra leadership responsibility on the ward
options.B: Basic salary and physical working conditions
options.C: Personal growth through advanced clinical training
options.D: Public recognition for an outstanding award

explanation: Hygiene factors prevent job dissatisfaction and include basic needs like fair pay, safe environment, and job security. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is a common cultural barrier that stops some communities from accepting routine immunization?

options.A: Strict laws banning children from entering clinics
options.B: The requirement that children must fast before vaccination
options.C: False rumors about vaccine safety and fertility
options.D: A mandatory tax placed on every vaccine dose

explanation: Great thinking! Baseless fears regarding side effects, like fertility issues, are major cultural hurdles we encounter in practice.

question: How can strict cultural rules about modesty affect how women use healthcare services?

options.A: They eliminate the need for nurses to take a thorough patient history
options.B: They may prevent women from seeing male practitioners, delaying necessary care
options.C: They guarantee that women receive priority treatment in private clinics
options.D: They automatically improve health outcomes by reducing community exposure

explanation: If community rules say women can only be examined by female staff, a lack of female doctors at the local clinic can cause a dangerous delay in treatment.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended nursing approach when correcting common contraceptive myths?

options.A: Validating the client's underlying concerns
options.B: Insulting the client for believing rumors
options.C: Providing clear and accurate health facts
options.D: Explaining normal physiological side effects

explanation: Insulting clients creates a hostile environment and drives them away from formal healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: When are lab hormone tests usually needed to confirm menopause?

options.A: In younger women with suspected premature or surgical menopause
options.B: When a woman reports weight gain
options.C: In every healthy woman reaching age 50
options.D: Only when hot flashes are absent

explanation: Usually, menopause is diagnosed just by looking at a woman's age and missed periods, but lab tests help when it happens unexpectedly early.

question: Which of the following is a common challenge that stops nurses from sharing their research?

options.A: An overabundance of free time during shifts
options.B: Lack of funding for open-access publication fees
options.C: Hospitals forcing all nurses to publish weekly papers
options.D: Too many journals competing to publish clinical studies

explanation: Well done! Publishing fees can be quite expensive, which unfortunately blocks many nurses from getting their work out in open-access journals.

question: When do immediate complications of an abortion typically show up?

options.A: Between one and two weeks after the event
options.B: During the procedure or within the first 24 hours
options.C: Only after a subsequent pregnancy begins
options.D: Several months to years later

explanation: Think of 'immediate' as happening right away! These complications usually show up while the procedure is going on or within the first 24 hours.

question: What do we call a cancer that starts in the epithelial tissue lining body surfaces?

options.A: Sarcoma
options.B: Myeloma
options.C: Leukemia
options.D: Carcinoma

explanation: You're doing great! Carcinomas are the most common type of cancer because they start in the skin and the cells lining our internal organs and body surfaces.

question: Why are standard Alzheimer's drugs usually avoided or used carefully in Pick's disease?

options.A: They accelerate memory loss within the first week of use.
options.B: They interfere with routine blood pressure medications.
options.C: They do not target the underlying pathology and can worsen agitation.
options.D: They cause immediate and permanent paralysis of the lower limbs.

explanation: Alzheimer's medications don't help frontotemporal issues and can actually make behavioral outbursts worse. It's a great clinical pearl to remember for your exams!

question: Which of these is a healthy, adaptive way for a client to cope with a tough health diagnosis?

options.A: Relying heavily on unprescribed sedatives
options.B: Denying that the illness exists altogether
options.C: Focusing on remaining abilities and maintaining humor
options.D: Isolating oneself completely from family members

explanation: Finding ways to laugh, adapt, and focus on what they can still do helps clients roll with the punches. That's true resilience!

question: Which hormone is released by special cells in the heart when the heart walls get stretched too much?
