explanation: You nailed it! Leaning forward keeps blood out of the throat, and pinching the soft part of the nose puts direct pressure right where it's bleeding.

question: Why are hospitals and clinics hotspots for drug-resistant germs?

options.A: Doctors rarely wash their hands between surgical procedures
options.B: They bring together sick patients, heavy drug use, and diverse germs
options.C: Indoor air conditioning circulates sterile spores constantly
options.D: Hospital walls are built using materials that trap bacteria

explanation: Hospitals concentrate vulnerable people and plenty of antibiotics, creating a place where tough, resistant strains can easily thrive.

question: What is the main job of the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscle movements
options.B: Promoting digestion and nutrient absorption at rest
options.C: Regulating the body's internal temperature during sleep
options.D: Preparing the body for stressful or emergency situations

explanation: Think of the sympathetic system as your body's 'fight-or-flight' alarm. It gets you ready to act fast when danger or heavy stress shows up. You've got this!

question: Why would a doctor order a tympanometry test?

options.A: To test the patient's balance and coordination
options.B: To check middle ear function and detect fluid
options.C: To measure the electrical activity of the brain
options.D: To visualize the tiny bones of the inner ear directly

explanation: Tympanometry tests how well your eardrum moves when air pressure changes. It's great for spotting fluid or pressure issues behind the eardrum.

question: What hormone directly stimulates the initial growth and maturation of ovarian follicles?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is released by the pituitary gland to stimulate ovarian follicles to grow. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is regular kit auditing and replenishment essential for community health programs?

options.A: To keep the outer packaging looking clean and professional
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing bulk supplies
options.C: To comply with paperwork demands from hospital administrators
options.D: To ensure supplies are not expired when an emergency birth occurs

explanation: Emergency kits are useless if items have degraded, expired, or been removed, making routine stock checks vital for community readiness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h7)

question: When a large amount of fluid is being drained, what vital sign change must a nurse watch out for?

options.A: A sharp drop in blood pressure
options.B: An extremely slow breathing rate
options.C: A sudden spike in body temperature
options.D: A sudden increase in urine output

explanation: Taking out too much fluid too fast can make the patient's blood pressure crash. We always keep a close eye on this!

question: Why are grab bars installed in bathrooms for individuals with physical disabilities?

options.A: To block water from splashing onto the bathroom floor tiles
options.B: To hold towels and washcloths within easy reach of the bathing area
options.C: To serve as hanging storage for lightweight assistive devices
options.D: To provide stable support during transfers on and off the toilet or in the shower

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces combined with transfers make grab bars essential safety features for preventing falls. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why is it so powerful to involve traditional and religious leaders in your public health campaigns?

options.A: They hold high community trust, which greatly boosts local participation
options.B: They possess advanced medical degrees to treat complex diseases
options.C: They provide direct financial funding from international donors
options.D: They legally mandate citizens to buy private health insurance

explanation: People listen to their traditional and religious leaders! When these leaders endorse your immunization or health drive, the whole community is much more likely to show up.

question: What is one of the biggest advantages of using the team nursing model?

options.A: Every single staff member performs the exact same tasks
options.B: Cost-effective use of mixed staff cadres working together
options.C: Complete elimination of any need for supervision
options.D: Patients never have to interact with nursing assistants

explanation: Spot on! Team nursing lets hospitals blend different skill levels efficiently, making patient care well-organized and resourceful.

question: Why is targeting the infection reservoir considered the best way to break the chain of transmission?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for standard hand hygiene
options.B: It immediately destroys all known antibodies in human blood
options.C: It prevents patients from developing any chronic illnesses
options.D: It removes the source where the pathogen lives and multiplies

explanation: If you cut off the source where germs are living and breeding, the whole chain of infection falls apart right from the start. Smart nursing strategy!

question: What is the main job of satellite cells in our skeletal muscles?

options.A: To repair and regenerate damaged muscle fibers
options.B: To remove lactic acid buildup after heavy exercise
options.C: To store calcium ions needed for sliding filaments
options.D: To produce the nerve signals that trigger contraction

explanation: Satellite cells are like little standby repair crew members. When muscle gets injured, they jump in to help fix and rebuild it!

question: What do we call any environmental factor or substance that causes birth defects in an unborn baby?

options.A: Pathogen
options.B: Carcinogen
options.C: Teratogen
options.D: Allergen

explanation: Spot on! Teratogens are agents like certain drugs, radiation, or infections that can interfere with normal prenatal development. You're making great progress!

question: What is the name of the special G-protein that helps us taste sweet, bitter, and umami foods?

options.A: Calmodulin
options.B: Opsin
options.C: Gustducin
options.D: Transducin

explanation: Gustducin is the key G-protein tucked inside Type II taste cells that handles sweet, bitter, and savory signals.

question: What is the main goal of a nursing journal club in a hospital?

options.A: To raise money for the hospital's annual end-of-year party
options.B: To review and discuss recent research articles in a supportive setting
options.C: To punish nurses who make medication errors on the ward
options.D: To sell textbooks and medical equipment to patients

explanation: Journal clubs are fun and supportive! They help nurses build confidence in reading and discussing research papers together. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of staffing in healthcare management?

options.A: Filling every vacant desk in the hospital
options.B: Matching qualified staff with patient care needs
options.C: Lowering the budget spent on medical equipment
options.D: Reducing the total number of working hours for nurses

explanation: Staffing is fundamentally about putting the right number of skilled workers where they are needed to keep patients safe. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h1)

question: What is a key role for the nurse when caring for a patient dealing with sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Coordinating referrals and ensuring the patient transitions smoothly between specialists
options.B: Deciding which prescription drugs the pharmacy will stock
options.C: Diagnosing rare endocrine disorders without physician oversight
options.D: Performing advanced surgical procedures independently in the clinic

explanation: Nurses act as the bridge! We connect patients with the right specialists (like therapists or urologists) to make sure they get team-based, compassionate care.

question: What type of care approach is most effective when treating survivors of forced marriage?

options.A: Experimental surgical care
options.B: Strictly punitive care
options.C: Cosmetic dermatological care
options.D: Trauma-informed care

explanation: Trauma-informed care acknowledges the profound psychological impact of abuse and focuses on safety, trust, and empowerment for the survivor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h7)

question: A client comes back to the clinic three weeks after getting an IUD with severe lower belly pain, fever, and strange vaginal discharge. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The IUD completely falling out on its own
options.B: Simple iron deficiency anemia
options.C: A normal adjustment period to the device
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Fever, foul discharge, and severe lower abdominal pain are classic red flags for an ascending uterine infection like PID. Act fast and evaluate her!

question: How does a clinical ward nurse use epidemiological thinking during a shift?

options.A: By writing national health laws for the ministry of health
options.B: By performing complex statistical data entry for research journals
options.C: By noticing an increase in infections on the ward and looking for a common cause
options.D: By manufacturing new antibiotics in the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Everyday nurses use mini-epidemiology all the time! Whenever you notice a sudden cluster of similar infections on your ward and start searching for the source, that's epidemiological thinking.

question: What is another common name for cancellous bone?

options.A: Cortical bone
options.B: Compact bone
options.C: Spongy bone
options.D: Dense bone

explanation: You got this! Cancellous bone is often called spongy bone because if you look at it inside, it has a porous, honeycomb-like pattern just like a kitchen sponge.

question: What procedure is often needed if leftover placental tissue is causing ongoing postpartum sepsis?

options.A: Total abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: Appendectomy
options.C: Evacuation of the uterus
options.D: Bilateral tubal ligation

explanation: If dead placental tissue is trapped inside, antibiotics alone won't clear it. We need to gently clear out the uterus to help the mother heal.

question: Which family planning method category also helps protect against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal pills
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Permanent surgeries
options.D: Intrauterine devices

explanation: Only barrier methods like condoms physically block fluids, which stops both unwanted pregnancy AND pesky STIs. Pills and IUDs do not protect against infections!

question: A visitor bumps the bed and a weight bag touches the floor. What is your very first step?

options.A: Immediately remove the skull pins to prevent further injury
options.B: Document the incident and wait for the doctor's morning round
options.C: Call the physical therapist to readjust the entire bed frame
options.D: Ensure the rope is in the pulley and lift the weight so it hangs freely

explanation: Quick action is key! Just check the rope and make sure those weights are hanging freely again to keep the traction working.

question: What sudden change is a classic early warning sign that a home care patient's heart failure is getting worse?

options.A: An increased appetite for high-fiber green vegetables
options.B: A sudden weight gain of two pounds or more overnight
options.C: A gradual increase in daily physical exercise tolerance
options.D: An unexpected drop in resting daytime heart rate

explanation: Spot on! When the heart isn't pumping efficiently, fluid builds up fast. An overnight weight jump is one of the earliest red flags for worsening heart failure.

question: What should the nurse check when inspecting the dressing after the procedure?

options.A: Whether the skin has turned a pale yellow color
options.B: If the adhesive tape is completely waterproof
options.C: Signs of bleeding, swelling, or fluid leakage
options.D: The exact temperature of the bandage material

explanation: Spot on! Regular site checks ensure any bleeding or fluid leakage is caught and managed early.

question: A student practices passing a urinary catheter three times on a dummy before doing it on a real patient. What is this called?

options.A: Intrinsic motivational grading
options.B: Passive cognitive observation
options.C: Pedagogical dependency
options.D: Deliberate practice and skill repetition

explanation: Repeating a skill in a safe practice space builds your muscle memory and boosts your confidence for real clinical work.

question: Which finding at a pacemaker incision site should you report right away as a sign of infection?

options.A: Mild itching around the healing skin
options.B: Faint bruising fading to a yellow color
options.C: A small firm lump directly under the scar
options.D: Pus drainage and spreading redness

explanation: Pus and spreading redness are classic warning signs of an infection that needs prompt medical attention. Excellent clinical eye!

question: A patient on tiopronin calls reporting a sudden sore throat, fever, and skin rash. What should you advise?

options.A: Suggest taking an over-the-counter antihistamine and doubling the evening water intake
options.B: Tell the patient this is a normal harmless side effect that will resolve in a few days
options.C: Advise the patient to stop the medication and report to the clinic immediately for lab work
options.D: Recommend waiting until the next scheduled routine appointment next month

explanation: Fever, sore throat, and rash can be warning signs of a serious reaction or blood issue. It's always best to pause the drug and have the medical team check them right away!

question: Why must you check the literacy level of a community before choosing your IEC materials?

options.A: To decide which doctor will be assigned to lead the surgical ward
options.B: To calculate the exact financial budget required for the health outreach program
options.C: To determine how many textbooks need to be ordered for the local primary school
options.D: To ensure the community can actually read and understand written text if print is used

explanation: If a community struggles with reading, handing out text-heavy brochures won't work well. You'll want to use pictures, audio, or drama instead!

question: Which cooking method is best for keeping foods tender on a soft diet?

options.A: Dry roasting at high temperatures
options.B: Deep frying in vegetable oil
options.C: Steaming or braising with liquids
options.D: Charbroiling over an open flame

explanation: Moist cooking methods like steaming and braising break down tough food fibers, making them much easier to chew and swallow. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h4)

question: A junior nurse is told to do a dressing change a certain way simply because 'that is how we've always done it here.' What type of inquiry is this?

options.A: Traditional and authority-based inquiry
options.B: Randomized controlled testing
options.C: Empirical scientific inquiry
options.D: Systematic qualitative inquiry

explanation: Relying on past custom and instructions from senior staff without checking the literature is traditional and authority-based inquiry.

question: Who is primarily responsible for keeping track of surgical instruments and sponges in the operating room?

options.A: The anaesthetist and the operating room manager
options.B: The lead surgeon and the assistant surgeon
options.C: The circulator nurse and the scrub nurse
options.D: The central sterile supply department technician

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! The scrub nurse and circulator nurse double-team the counts to make sure nothing is left behind.

question: When is using a mucous membrane route (like sublingual or rectal) a lifesaver for a patient?

options.A: When the patient needs a subcutaneous injection
options.B: When the medication must bypass the skin entirely
options.C: When the patient is unable to swallow oral medications
options.D: When the drug requires slow digestion in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is too weak, drowsy, or vomiting too much to swallow pills, routes like under the tongue or rectally keep their treatment going smoothly.

question: A nurse walks into a room and notices a patient clutching their chest and breathing heavily. What category of the general survey does this fall under?

options.A: Personal hygiene
options.B: Level of consciousness
options.C: Nutritional status
options.D: Signs of distress

explanation: Clutching the chest and heavy breathing are immediate physical indicators of acute distress. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which immune cells are the main targets for HIV?

options.A: Red blood cells
options.B: Platelets
options.C: CD4+ T cells
options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: HIV specifically targets and weakens CD4+ T cells. You've got this!

question: Which body system uses chemical messengers (hormones) to drive all the body changes during puberty?

options.A: The lymphatic system
options.B: The nervous reflex arc
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The digestive enzyme network

explanation: Spot on! The endocrine system is our body's hormone-manufacturing network, releasing chemical messengers straight into the bloodstream to spark growth and development.

question: Why do nurses do a cultural assessment for patients?

options.A: To satisfy mandatory hospital paperwork requirements only
options.B: To convince the patient to adopt Western medical practices
options.C: To understand the patient's beliefs and values in order to provide individualized care
options.D: To determine the financial income of the patient's household

explanation: Wonderful! Cultural assessments help us respect our patients' traditions and beliefs, making sure our care fits their unique lifestyle.

question: When caring for a patient with a cast, why should a nurse assess the whole patient and not just stare at the injury?

options.A: To ensure the plaster cast does not get dirty or wet
options.B: To monitor for dangerous systemic changes affecting the whole body
options.C: To measure the exact length of the bone healing underneath
options.D: To check if the patient is taking their pain medication on time

explanation: A bone injury doesn't happen in isolation! It can trigger widespread reactions throughout the body, so looking at the big picture helps you catch complications early.

question: What is the best and most accurate lab test used to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?

options.A: Complete blood count with differential
options.B: Nucleic acid amplification test
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Routine urinalysis dipstick

explanation: Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) are top-tier because they spot the actual genetic material of the bacteria with high accuracy.

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when caring for a patient who has overdosed on drugs?

options.A: Maintaining airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Discussing long-term career goals and ambitions
options.C: Asking about their family background and history
options.D: Administering a harsh disciplinary warning

explanation: ABC comes first in every emergency! Keeping the patient breathing and stable is always the top priority.

question: Why do many women wait a long time before seeking help for a reproductive tract infection?

options.A: The infections frequently do not cause noticeable symptoms early on
options.B: Laboratory tests take several weeks to show any positive results
options.C: Antibiotics for these conditions are universally unavailable
options.D: Initial symptoms always present as severe systemic shock

explanation: Since many of these infections start off completely silent, women feel totally fine and have no idea they need to visit a clinic.

question: What is the main risk of breastfeeding when a mother is living with HIV?

options.A: Severe malnutrition in the nursing infant
options.B: Transmission of the virus through breast milk
options.C: Rapid maternal immune system collapse
options.D: Permanent loss of breast milk production

explanation: You've got this! While breast milk is packed with goodness, it can unfortunately pass the virus from an infected mum to her baby during feeding. Understanding this helps us support mums better!

question: As a nurse, what is the very first test you should expect or check when a patient comes in with delayed menses?

options.A: Serum pregnancy test
options.B: Hysterosalpingogram
options.C: Diagnostic laparoscopy
options.D: Endometrial biopsy

explanation: Always rule out pregnancy first! In any woman of childbearing age with a missed or late period, checking for pregnancy is the mandatory first step.

question: In a research study, what is the independent variable?

options.A: An unexpected error in data collection
options.B: The patient outcome being measured
options.C: The demographic profile of the participants
options.D: The intervention or cause being manipulated

explanation: The independent variable is the 'cause' or the treatment that you (the researcher) introduce to see what happens.

question: Why do public health teams evaluate immunization services?

options.A: To reduce the total number of required clinic visits
options.B: To increase the market price of new vaccines
options.C: To measure program performance and safety
options.D: To punish staff who miss vaccination targets

explanation: Evaluation is simply our way of checking if our vaccination programs are running safely and truly protecting our communities. You've got this!

question: What is the name of the thick, yellowish fluid the breasts produce in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: Foremilk
options.B: Lymph fluid
options.C: Colostrum
options.D: Mature milk

explanation: Colostrum is often called 'liquid gold'! It's packed with antibodies and nutrients, ready and waiting for the newborn.

question: What is the main purpose of tertiary prevention in nursing care?

options.A: Preventing complications in established chronic diseases
options.B: Curing genetic disorders before birth
options.C: Stopping healthy people from ever getting sick
options.D: Screening asymptomatic populations for hidden risk

explanation: Well done! Tertiary prevention steps in after a diagnosis to help patients manage their condition and avoid further complications.

question: Which embryonic structures need to develop and fuse properly to form a normal uterus?

options.A: Ovarian follicles
options.B: Müllerian ducts
options.C: Fallopian tubes
options.D: Wolffian ducts

explanation: Great job! The female reproductive tract forms during embryonic development when the Müllerian ducts fuse and the middle wall is resorbed. You've got this!

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes asks why they need to eat more fiber. How should you explain it?

options.A: Fiber slows down digestion, which helps prevent sharp blood sugar spikes after meals
options.B: Fiber increases blood sugar levels rapidly for quick energy
options.C: Fiber completely cures diabetes within a few days of eating it
options.D: Fiber replaces the need to ever take diabetes medication again

explanation: Great nursing communication! Fiber slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping those glucose levels nice and steady after eating.

question: What is the primary definition of dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Painful menstrual periods that interfere with daily activities
options.B: Infection of the uterine lining during the postpartum period
options.C: Abnormally heavy bleeding during the regular menstrual cycle
options.D: The complete absence of menstrual bleeding for over six months

explanation: Dysmenorrhoea specifically refers to painful menstruation that is severe enough to disrupt a person's normal daily routine. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h1)

question: What happens to the tiny coronary blood vessels when local waste products like adenosine pile up?

options.A: They constrict to stop bleeding.
options.B: They harden into rigid fibrous tubes.
options.C: They collapse from high pressure.
options.D: They dilate to increase blood flow.

explanation: Well done! Metabolic waste acts like a chemical green light, telling the blood vessels to relax and open wide so more oxygen can reach hardworking tissues.

question: A nurse gets a positive rapid malaria test for a pregnant woman in a remote village. What should happen next?

options.A: Tell her to return home and wait for the fever to disappear on its own
options.B: Initiate the appropriate anti-malarial treatment protocol immediately
options.C: Ignore the result because rapid tests are never accurate
options.D: Send her patient file directly to the international health organization

explanation: Testing is only helpful if we act on the results! Once malaria is confirmed, starting treatment right away keeps both mother and baby safe.

question: What is a primary responsibility of a community health nurse in preventing infectious diseases?

options.A: Manufacturing sterile surgical instruments in the clinic kitchen
options.B: Isolating entire towns when a single flu case is reported
options.C: Educating families on hygiene, sanitation, and vaccination
options.D: Prescribing high-dose antibiotics without consulting a doctor

explanation: Community nurses empower everyday people with the practical knowledge needed to stop infections at home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h8)

question: How should a nurse handle bed sheets that are stained with blood?

options.A: Handle them with minimal agitation and bag them securely
options.B: Wash them by hand in the patient bathroom sink
options.C: Leave them on the floor until housekeeping arrives
options.D: Shake them out thoroughly to remove loose debris

explanation: You nailed it! Shaking dirty linens sends dust and germs flying everywhere. Roll them up gently and bag them safely!

question: What common physical sensation do many patients report when experiencing a sudden heart dysrhythmia?

options.A: Muscle spasms
options.B: Abdominal cramps
options.C: Joint stiffness
options.D: Palpitations

explanation: Patients frequently feel palpitations, which they describe as a racing, skipping, or fluttering sensation in their chest. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do active tissues like tumors absorb large amounts of FDG during a PET scan?

options.A: Rapidly dividing cells require high amounts of energy and glucose.
options.B: Cancer cells have abnormal blood vessels that block normal water flow.
options.C: The radioactive tracer binds directly to the DNA strands of damaged cells.
options.D: Tumors actively attract and trap radioactive metal inside their walls.

explanation: Exactly! Because cancer cells grow and multiply so fast, they need a ton of energy. Since FDG acts just like glucose, the tumor sucks it right up, making it glow brightly on the scan.

question: What happens if a caregiver mixes an ORS sachet in way too little water?

options.A: The child will refuse to drink because the solution is too cold
options.B: The extra salt crystals will kill all the bacteria in the stomach
options.C: The concentrated solution can worsen dehydration by drawing water into the gut
options.D: The medicine works twice as fast to stop the watery stool

explanation: Measurements matter! Too little water makes the drink too salty (hypertonic), which actually pulls body water out into the intestines and makes dehydration worse.

question: Why is it important to document family planning care immediately after the encounter?

options.A: To ensure the client stays in the waiting room longer
options.B: To satisfy administrative rules without clinical benefit
options.C: To prevent forgetting important details and clinical observations
options.D: To allow other clients to read the previous notes

explanation: Immediate documentation ensures accuracy because details about blood pressure, client questions, and specific instructions are still fresh in mind. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h4)

question: What is the main difference between pitting and non-pitting oedema?

options.A: Pitting oedema only occurs on the face, while non-pitting oedema only affects the feet.
options.B: Pitting oedema leaves an indentation after pressure, while non-pitting oedema does not.
options.C: Pitting oedema is always painless, whereas non-pitting oedema causes severe sharp pain.
options.D: Pitting oedema disappears with rest, while non-pitting oedema requires surgery.

explanation: Spot on! It's all in the name. Pitting leaves a little thumbprint depression because the fluid shifts easily, whereas non-pitting (often linked to lymphatic issues) stays firm.

question: A resident says they already took their morning blood pressure pill, but the medication administration record (MAR) is blank for that time. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a second dose immediately to ensure their blood pressure stays controlled
options.B: Wait until the evening shift to see if the blood pressure spikes
options.C: Assume the resident is correct and sign the record as given by the resident
options.D: Withhold the dose and consult the prescribing physician or charge nurse before acting

explanation: Brilliant! Giving a double dose can be dangerous. Always pause, check the facts, and consult your senior colleagues or doctor when something doesn't match up.

question: A patient walks out of a dark cinema into the bright afternoon sun and squints before seeing clearly. What is this quick adjustment called?

options.A: Pupillary constriction
options.B: Dark adaptation
options.C: Light adaptation
options.D: Corneal refraction

explanation: This is light adaptation—your eyes quickly recalibrate when stepping from darkness into bright sunlight. You're smashing it!

question: Which part of the Glasgow Coma Scale is usually seen as the best clue to how well a patient will recover?

options.A: Verbal response
options.B: Pupillary reflex
options.C: Motor response
options.D: Eye opening

explanation: The motor response checks deep brain pathways. It gives nurses and doctors the strongest clue about how a patient is recovering after a head injury.

question: Why do nurses prefer to use a clear, transparent dressing over an IV insertion site?

options.A: It completely stops the patient from feeling any accidental movement pain.
options.B: It allows the nurse to inspect the skin for redness without removing the cover.
options.C: It keeps the cannula warm so the IV fluid flows much faster.
options.D: It permanently seals the vein shut so no blood can ever leak out.

explanation: Spot on! Clear dressings keep outside germs away while letting you quickly check the site for early signs of swelling or redness without peeling anything back.

question: A nurse wants to document the exact number of malaria cases in a clinic last month. Which study type fits best?

options.A: Experimental laboratory design
options.B: Descriptive design
options.C: Explanatory design
options.D: Exploratory design

explanation: Correct! When you are just describing what is happening naturally without testing causes, it's a descriptive study.

question: A patient says she does not want her partner to visit because she is scared of his reaction. What should you do?

options.A: Insist that family presence is mandatory for hospital discharge clearance
options.B: Call the partner immediately to inform him of her hospital admission
options.C: Respect her wishes, maintain confidentiality, and protect her from visitors
options.D: Ask the hospital security team to convince the client to change her mind

explanation: As a nurse, your primary loyalty is to protect your patient's safety and honor her personal boundaries.

question: What three core elements are typically included in a community diagnosis statement?

options.A: The political party in power, the village chief, and tax rates
options.B: The weather forecast, the road network, and transport costs
options.C: The health problem, the affected population, and the contributing factors
options.D: The name of the nurse, the hospital budget, and drug expiration dates

explanation: A complete community diagnosis clearly names the issue, who is suffering from it, and why it is happening. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h4)

question: Think of a theoretical framework as the backbone of a nursing study. What is its main job?

options.A: Providing funding for data collection and equipment
options.B: Serving as the structural foundation and guide for the study
options.C: Determining the exact sample size needed for the project
options.D: Writing the final reference list in the correct format

explanation: Spot on! Just like a physical building needs a strong frame to stand, a research study needs a theoretical framework to shape how it is designed and understood.

question: When applying a temporary splint to a suspected fracture, which joints should you include?

options.A: Only the single joint closest to the end of the broken bone
options.B: Only the joint directly below the location of the break
options.C: The joints immediately above and below the fracture site
options.D: Every single joint located throughout the entire injured limb

explanation: Spot on! To truly keep a broken bone stable, you must immobilize the joints right above and right below it. This stops the bone ends from shifting and protects the nearby tissues.

question: How often should you flush a continuous feeding NG tube with water to keep it clear?

options.A: Immediately after every shift change
options.B: Every 4 to 6 hours
options.C: Only when the patient coughs
options.D: Once every 48 hours

explanation: Flushing every 4 to 6 hours keeps the formula from drying out and blocking the tube. Regular maintenance keeps things flowing smoothly!

question: When is the exact right time to chart a medication you just gave?

options.A: At the end of the entire nursing shift
options.B: Whenever the prescribing doctor asks for updates
options.C: Before preparing the drug at the medication cart
options.D: Immediately after the patient swallows the drug

explanation: Always chart right away after giving it! This stops another nurse from accidentally giving a double dose.

question: A patient is scared to name their coworkers because they are worried about losing their job. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Threaten to report the patient to the local police force for withholding data
options.B: Assure the patient of strict confidentiality and explain the public health goal
options.C: Tell the employer immediately so other workers can be screened by force
options.D: Skip asking about coworkers and only record family members living at home

explanation: Building trust is key in nursing. Reassuring them that their information is private helps them feel safe to share what we need to keep the community healthy.

question: Which insect transmits the parasite responsible for malaria?

options.A: Housefly
options.B: Tsetse fly
options.C: Female Anopheles mosquito
options.D: Blackfly

explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted specifically through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h5)

question: What happens when someone mixes sleeping pills (sedatives) with alcohol?

options.A: Immediate neutralization of all toxic chemicals in the blood
options.B: A sudden increase in physical stamina and alertness
options.C: Severe respiratory suppression and potential breathing failure
options.D: Enhanced absorption of vital nutrients in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Both alcohol and sedatives slow down the brain. Combining them can make breathing slow down to a dangerous, fatal stop.

question: Where would a nurse expect to find sinusoid capillaries with large gaps in their walls?

options.A: In the walls of skeletal muscles
options.B: In the continuous lining of the brain
options.C: In the liver and bone marrow
options.D: In the outer layer of human skin

explanation: Sinusoids feature large intercellular gaps that allow the passage of whole blood cells, which is essential in organs like the liver, spleen, and bone marrow. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why do clinics use more than one test (an algorithm) instead of just one rapid test for a positive result?

options.A: To make the testing process longer and more thorough
options.B: To ensure diagnostic accuracy and prevent misdiagnosis
options.C: To use up excess laboratory supplies before they expire
options.D: To comply with insurance billing requirements for hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Running sequential tests confirms initial results so we protect clients from the heavy emotional blow of a false positive.

question: What is a major risk of mixing herbal products with HIV medications without asking a doctor?

options.A: They turn the medicine into harmless sugar water
options.B: They always cure the infection faster
options.C: They have zero effect on drugs
options.D: They can dangerously lower drug levels in the blood

explanation: Correct! Some herbs mess with liver enzymes, clearing out life-saving medications too quickly and making them less effective.

question: What is a sample in a research study?

options.A: A small subset of people chosen to represent a larger population
options.B: A chemical substance tested in a laboratory beaker
options.C: The final written report published in a journal
options.D: The budget allocated for purchasing hospital supplies

explanation: Researchers study a sample because it is usually impossible to measure every single person in a target population. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h4)

question: In the popular PICOT research framework, what does the letter 'I' stand for?

options.A: Institution
options.B: Infection
options.C: Investigation
options.D: Intervention

explanation: The 'I' stands for Intervention. It represents the specific treatment, action, or care practice you are testing out in your study.

question: Why do health workers treat gender-based violence as a major public health emergency?

options.A: It only affects women living in rural environments
options.B: It primarily places financial strain on hospital pharmacies
options.C: It causes widespread physical and psychological harm across communities
options.D: It is classified as a rare infectious disease outbreak

explanation: You got it! Because it hurts so many people physically and emotionally, healthcare systems treat it as a top priority to keep communities safe.

question: What is the main job of self-tolerance in our immune system?

options.A: To prevent the immune system from attacking healthy body tissue
options.B: To destroy foreign invaders like bacteria and viruses
options.C: To increase the production of red blood cells
options.D: To help white blood cells mature in the lymph nodes

explanation: Think of self-tolerance as the immune system's security check. It helps white blood cells recognize our own body parts so they don't mistakenly attack healthy organs!

question: Which two major organs take the heaviest hit from long-term, uncontrolled high blood pressure?

options.A: Liver and pancreas
options.B: Heart and kidneys
options.C: Lungs and stomach
options.D: Spleen and thyroid

explanation: Because the heart and kidneys are packed with delicate blood vessels, they bear the brunt of constant high pressure, leading to heart and kidney failure over time.

question: How should a nurse handle someone who argues that there is 'no budget' for a new health project?

options.A: Ignore the stakeholder completely and proceed without their approval
options.B: Provide evidence showing financial losses caused by ignoring the issue
options.C: Offer to pay for the entire project out of the nurse's own salary
options.D: Argue loudly that the government is corrupt and does not care

explanation: Smart move! Showing them how much money the problem is *already* costing them helps turn a 'no budget' excuse into a reason to invest.

question: What is the most serious and dangerous complication that can happen after a gastrointestinal dilation?

options.A: Mild throat irritation
options.B: Temporary hiccups
options.C: Visceral perforation
options.D: Dry mouth sensation

explanation: Perforation means a tear or hole gets poked through the wall of the esophagus or bowel. It's a medical emergency that happens if the tissue tears during stretching.

question: A nurse in a rural Nigerian health post is triaging multiple patients with fever and cough. Why is pulse oximetry especially useful here?

options.A: It quickly identifies silent hypoxia requiring urgent oxygen therapy
options.B: It cures the underlying lung infection without medications
options.C: It replaces the need to check the patient's respiratory rate
options.D: It gives a definitive diagnosis of bacterial pneumonia

explanation: Pulse oximetry helps nurses spot dangerous drops in blood oxygen before physical symptoms like severe blue lips become obvious. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h4)

question: At 34 weeks, an antenatal patient is found to have a soft heart murmur. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Immediately send the patient to the emergency operating theatre
options.B: Recognize it as a common normal finding due to increased blood volume
options.C: Order emergency blood transfusions to correct severe anemia
options.D: Diagnose the patient with permanent rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood flow and heart position changes often cause harmless murmurs during pregnancy. No need to panic!

question: What happens to a mother's body when her diet lacks proper nutrition during pregnancy?

options.A: Maternal blood volume increases beyond normal limits
options.B: The fetus draws nutrients from the mother's own body stores
options.C: Fetal growth remains completely unaffected by maternal diet
options.D: The placenta stops growing completely to save energy

explanation: When food intake is low, the clever baby takes what it needs from your own body reserves! This is why mums can feel so drained. You're doing great learning how the body adapts.

question: A mother brings in her baby who has had watery diarrhea for two days, looks very sleepy (lethargic), and has sunken eyes. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Measure the child's height and head circumference
options.B: Administer a routine measles vaccine immediately
options.C: Send the mother home with advice to wait another week
options.D: Assess hydration status and prepare for urgent medical referral

explanation: Spot on! Lethargy and sunken eyes mean severe dehydration, which can turn dangerous very quickly. They need urgent fluid care and a doctor's help right away.

question: Why do regular antibiotics like standard penicillin fail against tuberculosis?

options.A: Penicillin only works on viruses, and TB is a fungus
options.B: Human stomach acid destroys penicillin before it reaches the lungs
options.C: The waxy outer cell wall of TB blocks standard drugs from entering
options.D: Tuberculosis bacteria move too fast for penicillin to catch them

explanation: TB bacteria have a tough, waxy outer coat that standard antibiotics just can't break through. That's why special anti-TB drugs are a must!

question: What is the most common and trusted way to sterilize metal surgical tools?

options.A: Boiling in water for twenty minutes
options.B: Steam under pressure in an autoclave
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation in a glass cabinet
options.D: Immersion in liquid bleach solution

explanation: The autoclave is the workhorse of the CSSD! Using high-pressure steam is fast, affordable, and extremely reliable for metal instruments.

question: When should the rehabilitation journey ideally start for a patient who has suffered a major injury?

options.A: When the patient asks to start walking
options.B: Only after the patient is discharged home
options.C: As soon as the patient is medically stable
options.D: After all chronic complications develop

explanation: Rehab starts early—right after the patient is medically stable—to prevent stiffness and get a head start on recovery.

question: In simple terms, what is atelectasis?

options.A: An abnormal collection of air in the pleural cavity
options.B: A severe bacterial infection inside the lung tissue
options.C: The collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced gas exchange
options.D: High pressure inside the blood vessels of the lungs

explanation: Correct! Atelectasis happens when tiny air sacs (alveoli) deflate or collapse, making it harder to trade gases.

question: During a community disease outbreak, what is one of the main duties of a nurse?

options.A: Manufacturing new vaccines in the local clinic
options.B: Conducting contact tracing and health education
options.C: Prescribing experimental drugs without supervision
options.D: Changing national health budget allocations

explanation: As a nurse, you are a community educator and detective! You track down contacts and teach families how to stay safe and stop the spread.

question: When starting a heart failure patient on a new beta-blocker, what is the safest way to begin?

options.A: Give the drug only when the patient has chest pain
options.B: Start with a very low dose and increase it gradually
options.C: Give a high loading dose to get quick protection
options.D: Stop all other heart failure medications immediately

explanation: Exactly! Because beta-blockers can temporarily slow things down too much when first introduced, our golden nursing rule is always: 'start low and go slow.'

question: Which of the following diseases is closely linked to poor environmental sanitation and stagnant water around schools?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Rickets
options.C: Cataracts
options.D: Scurvy

explanation: Cholera and other waterborne or vector-borne illnesses thrive when sanitation and drainage around schools are poor. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why must you mention pending lab tests or investigations during a shift report?

options.A: To prove to the hospital management that tests are expensive
options.B: So the patient can decide whether to cancel the appointment
options.C: So the incoming nurse can monitor preparation and follow up on results
options.D: To ensure the laboratory staff receive extra break time

explanation: Tests often need special preparation before and tracking after, which becomes the job of the incoming shift.

question: What are the two main parts that make up a patient's overall level of consciousness?

options.A: Speech and memory
options.B: Reflexes and coordination
options.C: Arousal and awareness
options.D: Strength and sensation

explanation: Consciousness is all about being awake (arousal) and being able to interact with your surroundings and thoughts (awareness). Both are essential!

question: What is the most common active chemical found in modern spermicides?

options.A: Chlorhexidine
options.B: Hydrogen peroxide
options.C: Nonoxynol-9
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: Correct! Nonoxynol-9 is the trusty chemical agent added to gels and foams to target and destroy sperm cell membranes.

question: What is a major bottleneck when trying to execute the Nigerian health budget?

options.A: Delayed release of approved funds by treasury authorities
options.B: Excessive availability of cash at the primary clinic level
options.C: Automatic approval of all health sector requests
options.D: Complete absence of legislative review

explanation: Even when a budget looks great on paper, getting the actual cash released to clinics often takes a frustratingly long time.

question: A patient just took a morning injection of regular (short-acting) insulin. When should the nurse watch out for the highest risk of low blood sugar?

options.A: Twelve to twenty-four hours after injection
options.B: Two to three hours after injection
options.C: Ten minutes after injection
options.D: Immediately upon skin puncture

explanation: You got it! Short-acting insulin usually peaks around 2 to 3 hours, meaning that's when blood sugar drops the fastest and needs close monitoring.

question: How do biologic drugs help patients dealing with severe autoimmune skin conditions?

options.A: By acting as a physical shield on the skin surface to block sunlight
options.B: By numbing sensory nerve fibers so the patient no longer feels itchy
options.C: By completely destroying all white blood cells circulating in the bloodstream
options.D: By specifically targeting and blocking certain parts of the overactive immune system

explanation: Brilliant! Biologics are smart medications that zero in on specific overactive immune signals to calm inflammation down precisely.

question: What is the main goal of cross-matching blood before a transfusion?

options.A: To determine the exact hemoglobin level of the donor blood
options.B: To detect any active reaction between donor cells and recipient serum
options.C: To warm the blood to body temperature before it leaves the lab
options.D: To check if the donor has a history of infectious diseases

explanation: Cross-matching is like a compatibility test in a tube. We mix the patient's blood with the donor's to make sure they play nicely together before it ever reaches the vein!

question: What is the main goal of medications called inotropes in acute heart failure?

options.A: To increase the strength of the heart's muscle contractions
options.B: To stop all electrical activity in the heart
options.C: To dissolve stubborn stomach ulcers
options.D: To lower body temperature during a fever

explanation: Inotropes act like a personal gym coach for the heart muscle, helping it squeeze harder so it can push more blood out to the body when it's struggling.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core pillars of safe motherhood?

options.A: Postnatal care
options.B: Family planning
options.C: Mandatory retirement
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Easy pick! The real pillars are family planning, antenatal care, safe delivery care, and postnatal care.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason to call a Rapid Response Team?

options.A: A sudden drop in oxygen saturation
options.B: Unexplained chest pain or pressure
options.C: A patient complaining of mild boredom
options.D: A sudden decrease in mental alertness

explanation: You've got this! Feeling bored is uncomfortable, but it isn't an emergency. Oxygen drops, chest pain, and sudden confusion, however, are major warning signs that need immediate backup!

question: Why must a pharmacy balance full cost recovery with making drugs affordable?

options.A: To prevent private pharmacies from suing the hospital for unfair competition
options.B: To ensure the doctors receive a bonus for prescribing cheaper medications
options.C: To comply with international laws governing pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.D: To make sure vulnerable patients can still afford their essential treatments

explanation: If drug prices climb too high, everyday patients won't be able to buy them, which defeats the whole public health mission of our hospitals.

question: Which tool do nurses use to hold and guide a suture needle securely through the skin?

options.A: Suture scissors
options.B: Needle holder
options.C: Tissue forceps
options.D: Scalpel handle

explanation: Spot on! A needle holder has special grip jaws built to hold a curved needle firmly so it doesn't slip or bend while you work.

question: Why do maternity nurses need to know baby skull anatomy well?

options.A: It helps assess foetal position and monitor labour progress
options.B: It allows the nurse to calculate the exact date of conception
options.C: It determines whether the mother will need a blood transfusion
options.D: It prevents the need for any internal pelvic examinations

explanation: Spot on! By feeling the landmarks on the baby's head during vaginal exams, you can tell which way the baby is facing and how well labor is moving along.

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.B: Before entering a patient room for vital signs
options.C: After touching an intact patient gown
options.D: Immediately before administering oral medication

explanation: Alcohol rubs do not clean away physical dirt or certain spore-forming bacteria effectively, requiring mechanical washing with soap and water. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which animal is known as the natural reservoir host for the Ebola virus?

options.A: Pigs on farms
options.B: Domestic dogs
options.C: Fruit bats
options.D: Cattle and goats

explanation: Spot on! Fruit bats carry the virus naturally without getting sick themselves. Think of them as the original home of the virus in nature.

question: When would a nurse most likely need to check a primary literature source?

options.A: When looking up the standard adult dose of paracetamol for a headache
options.B: When checking the common side effects of routine oral antibiotics
options.C: When searching for newly published clinical trial results on a novel cancer drug
options.D: When verifying the route of administration for an intravenous fluid

explanation: Exactly! Primary sources are original research studies. You go to them when you need the absolute newest, raw findings that haven't made it into textbooks yet.

question: Why is environmental sustainability included as a core goal of food policy?

options.A: To reduce the total volume of crops grown worldwide
options.B: To prevent farmers from ever using modern machinery
options.C: To ensure that agricultural land is turned into housing estates
options.D: To protect soil and water resources for future food production

explanation: Sustainability ensures that farming practices do not ruin the environment, allowing continuous food production over the long term. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)
